title: [GMCP 203.016.05] Interoperability and quality: First-class extension framework and extension governance
goal: Requirement GMCP-203-016-05. Prove applicable official-suite and reference-SDK interoperability in both roles, direct-versus-gateway differential behavior, property invariants, transport and platform parity, and published latency, throughput, startup, memory, disk, and fairness budgets. Retain regression fixtures for every incompatibility found. Vector outcome: Namespaced MCP extensions can be discovered, negotiated, configured, versioned, isolated and disabled through one typed framework without forking core protocol code. Unknown extensions round-trip safely, required unsupported extensions fail explicitly, official and experimental status is visible, collision and downgrade rules are enforced, and a watch process opens roadmap work for every newly published official extension. Done means production-path tests and retained evidence prove this work package; task closure or roadmap wording alone is not evidence.
limitations: Server-role extension advertisement, unknown-key preservation, isolation, and dynamic disablement run on shipped GmcpService, StdioGate, HTTP /mcp, embedded_adapter, and Unix sockets (#[cfg(unix)]); on Windows x86_64, Unix socket parity is gated #[cfg(unix)] while stdio, embedded, and Streamable HTTP run directly.

Client-role capability/extension exchange is verified through susi_wire_client::mcp::Session (open_with_capabilities, server_capabilities, server_extensions) plus ExtensionRegistry::negotiate and susi_core::mcp_client against live gateway and reference HTTP servers; implicit unknown-extension acceptance follows EXT-002 unless callers pass required extension lists to ExtensionRegistry::negotiate.
Phase 1 keeps T-CODEXGMCPROADMAP-83 open prior to Phase 2 closure; VC-203-016 operations and signed evidence retention belong to T-CODEXGMCPROADMAP-84 and T-CODEXGMCPROADMAP-85.

reuse.reason: Reused shipped ExtensionRegistry, CanonicalContentBlock, ExtensionCapabilities, RequestMetaObject, GmcpService, StdioGate, HTTP /mcp gateway, susi_core::mcp_client, and acceptance adapters in Susi Core, adding only Session::open_with_capabilities, Session::server_capabilities, and Session::server_extensions in crates/susi-wire-client/src/mcp.rs so the Wire SDK client retains peer capabilities.extensions from initialize.
